text: Table 2 reports honest-player win rates without precommit of 59.7% (4 pixels) and 74.4% (6 pixels), averaged over which player moves first, compared with 85.2% and 88.9% with precommit; without precommit the liar wins on any incorrect judge guess. The caption states that with or without precommit the honest player wins more often than 'a random judge', which the authors read as showing that honesty has an advantage.
title: MNIST debate without precommit: smaller honest-player advantage (Table 2)
